name: E Factor Experiences Limited
sector: Public experiences, events, museums and adventure tourism
summary: E Factor Experiences designs and executes public experiences, events and tourism projects. Its demonstrated access to complex projects is a strength: FY2026 revenue reached ₹191.44 crore, representing 17.09% annual growth since FY2023. The decisive weakness is cash realization: three profitable years generated cumulative CFO of −₹17.15 crore against ₹55.21 crore of group PAT. This is a project-led growth thesis, not an established cash-compounding franchise. At the 19 October 2026 close of ₹204.55, a conditional five-year base model returns 10.94%, below the 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle; the ordinary bear case loses 55.45% of capital. BQS 5.04, GQS 5.70 before a persistent-cash-weakness cap of 5.00, and IAS 3.71 imply ‘Weak setup / value-trap risk’. This is not a finding of fraud or imminent insolvency. Better collections, verified funding capacity and a less demanding price or stronger economics would change the assessment. [S1][S2][S3][S16]

gates.reason: No substantiated integrity failure was found in reviewed sources. Related-party transactions, historical filing/restatement issues and recovery litigation require context, not allegations. Audited disclosures were reviewed; this is not a guarantee against undiscovered issues.

Group cash flow reconciles and obligations are mapped. Original and IPO-restated history are kept separate; group profit, owner attribution and ancillary tax-note presentation are not silently combined. No material unexplained group cash deficit is identified. The model uses March audited balances conditionally, not a verified October balance sheet.

No lender default is reported. Base and ordinary bear cases repay annual-end debt; severe stress requires ₹77.57 crore against a ₹40 crore analyst reference, not a confirmed credit limit. No rescue or guaranteed refinancing is assumed. Current limits and intra-year peaks remain unverified, so severe-stress survival is not certified. That uncertainty alone is not demonstrated current default.

Official 19 October trades and eligible SM status support historical tradability. The 400-share lot and alerts effective 21 October constrain execution. Historical turnover cannot establish current depth or guaranteed exit. IAS remains conditional on the illustrative ₹5 lakh reference.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: E Factor Experiences designs and executes public experiences, events and tourism projects. Its demonstrated access to complex projects is a strength: FY2026 revenue reached ₹191.44 crore, representing 17.09% annual growth since FY2023. The decisive weakness is cash realization: three profitable years generated cumulative CFO of −₹17.15 crore against ₹55.21 crore of group PAT. This is a project-led growth thesis, not an established cash-compounding franchise. At the 19 October 2026 close of ₹204.55, a conditional five-year base model returns 10.94%, below the 15% nominal pretax equity hurdle; the ordinary bear case loses 55.45% of capital. BQS 5.04, GQS 5.70 before a persistent-cash-weakness cap of 5.00, and IAS 3.71 imply ‘Weak setup / value-trap risk’. This is not a finding of fraud or imminent insolvency. Better collections, verified funding capacity and a less demanding price or stronger economics would change the assessment. [S1][S2][S3][S16]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Research cutoff: 20 October 2026. Market endpoint: 19 October, before the 20 October holiday. Identity: E Factor Experiences Limited, NSE SME symbol EFACTOR, ISIN INE0KFF01017. Issued shares of 13,131,398 multiplied by ₹204.55 give market capitalization of ₹268.60 crore. The latest audited financial scope is consolidated FY2026 under Indian GAAP/AS, not Ind AS. Adventure Tourism is 61.57%-owned; Untamed is an associate, not a wholly owned operating division. The model covers 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, using audited 31 March 2026 balances as a conditional opening proxy. It does not invent unpublished intervening profits, collections or obligations. The equity hurdle is 15%, not WACC. The ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is illustrative, not the user’s allocation. Confidence is High on inspected primary financial totals and dated market rows, and Medium on growth mix, incremental returns, current funding and minority valuation. Overall confidence is Medium. The four gate conclusions are conditional passes or passes with caveats, with detailed reasons in the gate register. [S1][S4][S6][S15][S16]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 7, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 5, EXEC 5 and EARN 5. IAS factors are R 3, D 3, P 4 and L 4. BQS = 1.00 + 1.00 + 0.84 + 0.60 + 0.60 + 0.20 + 0.40 + 0.40 = 5.04. GQS = 2.80 + 1.20 + 0.75 + 0.75 + 0.20 = 5.70, capped at 5.00 because poor cash conversion persists across profitable years, not merely one temporary build. IAS = 0.25×5.04 + 0.35×3 + 0.20×3 + 0.10×4 + 0.10×4 = 3.71. Each composite has full factor coverage, which is not certainty about forecasts. Display values are 5.0, 5.0 and 3.7; unrounded values govern classification. Factor audits include supporting and contrary evidence. No historical factor receives 9–10; Medium confidence would cap it at 8 even with an extreme headline CAGR. These research conventions are not empirically validated return predictors. [S1][S2][S3][S16]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: The parent designs and delivers government and tourism events, cultural experiences, museums, installations and private events. Contract revenue requires design, procurement, vendor coordination and on-site delivery, often before final customer collections. Adventure Tourism operates balloon experiences under SkyWaltz; the associate is not added proportionately to operating revenue. Contracts can combine installation and later operation: the Kanjli award provides 12 months for execution and five years of O&M. The Wardha museum/statue order was ₹10.53012 crore with a 180-day execution period; completion and payment have not been independently confirmed. DS Group’s ₹5 crore Shiva sponsorship is commercial support, not equity proceeds or proof of project profit. Government customers supplied 89.55%, 93.26% and 79.23% of revenue in FY2023, FY2022 and FY2021 respectively; those historical percentages are not asserted to describe FY2026. Current top-customer and top-vendor concentration was not located. FY2026 service costs were ₹141.97 crore, or 74.16% of revenue, against 75 permanent employees. This supports an outsourced execution model rather than a large owned factory. Pricing and vendor discipline matter more than a generic asset-light label. [S1][S4][S7][S8][S9]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Qualification credentials, design capability and delivery experience can improve access to complex public projects. The two dated museum/tourism awards corroborate that access. They do not establish sole-source pricing, contractual customer lock-in or strong switching costs. Historical fixed-price tenders often lacked escalation, leaving cost and delay risk with the operator. Government budgets and tender outcomes also reduce recurrence. Adjacent competitors have different mixes: Touchwood emphasizes weddings and private/corporate events; Exhicon emphasizes exhibitions and event services; Mach markets corporate travel and MICE alongside broader travel solutions. These are qualitative product comparisons, not interchangeable valuation peers or rankings of audited quality. E Factor’s public-experience focus differentiates its business, but verified market share and sustained price premiums are absent. Its advantages could weaken through lost qualification access, creative-personnel turnover, vendor failures or the financing burden of collections. MOAT 5 therefore recognizes useful but contestable capability. [S4][S7][S8][S21][S22][S23]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Reported revenue, in ₹ crore, was 6.2162 in FY2021, 56.6155 in FY2022, 119.2616 in FY2023, 148.5574 in FY2024, 171.5537 in FY2025 and 191.4405 in FY2026. Five-year CAGR of 98.45% is dominated by the pandemic shutdown base. It is shown but not used as evidence of sustainable near-100% growth. The chosen FY2023–FY2026 window gives 17.09% CAGR and is more relevant to normalized expansion. Annual additions in FY2024, FY2025 and FY2026 were ₹29.2958, ₹22.9963 and ₹19.8868 crore, corresponding to growth of 24.56%, 15.48% and 11.59%. This is deceleration, not contraction. No material acquired revenue stream was identified in the inspected history, but a precise organic/price/volume bridge is not disclosed. FY2023 revenue agrees between the original annual comparator and IPO restatement, whereas profits and CFO differ and are kept separate. REV starts at 7 with no extra small-base penalty or bonus for future pipeline. The latest slowdown does not by itself justify an additional trajectory adjustment without the framework’s sustained comparable evidence. [S1][S2][S3][S4]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Accessible opportunities include public experiences, museums, installations and ongoing operations, plus sponsored commercial experiences. Wardha, Kanjli and DS Group provide dated evidence of access. Management’s ₹500–550 crore pipeline is not binding backlog: cancellation rights, advances, margins and remaining execution are not fully reconciled. The base model uses successive post-entry annual revenue of ₹229.73, ₹264.19, ₹295.89, ₹325.48 and ₹351.52 crore, with growth of 20%, 15%, 12%, 10% and 8%. The first period is not an FY2027 forecast, though it is less aggressive than management’s ₹300–325 crore FY2027 target. The terminal run rate needs ₹160.08 crore more annual business than FY2026; the named orders are not added again. Actual opening receivable and other operating-asset ratios are preserved, normal payables scale consistently, collateral is funded, and cash capex is 2.5% of revenue. Five periods require ₹36.67 crore of capex and ₹64.26 crore of incremental operating working capital. At a 14% EBITDA margin, normalized tax and explicit debt costs, the base annual cash sweep is manageable. Collection deterioration nevertheless pushes debt above the illustrative ₹40 crore envelope. Growth therefore has a substantial funding requirement, and mixed incremental returns plus persistent weak conversion cap GQS at 5. [S1][S5][S7][S8][S9][S11]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The 1 June 2026 call acknowledged FY2026 revenue of ₹191.44 crore against a prior ₹225–240 crore target. Management attributed about ₹35 crore to delayed February–March events, referring to weather and West Asia disruption. Subsequent execution of those events is not yet verified; the miss is not evidence of intentional misguidance. FY2027 revenue of ₹300–325 crore and FY2030 revenue of ₹1,000 crore remain management targets, not analyst forecasts. The April Wardha award had a 180-day schedule, while September’s Kanjli award allows 12 months, so neither can simply be recognized immediately. IPO proceeds of ₹25.92 crore included ₹13 crore for working capital, ₹3.5 crore for debt repayment and ₹2 crore for subsidiary investment. The last amount remained unutilized at March 2026: disclosed delayed deployment, not proven misuse. FY2026 director remuneration totaled ₹1.9022 crore and salary to a relative ₹0.06 crore. A prior FY2025 fixed-asset sale to Jai Kumar Thakore for ₹1.75 crore is disclosed; an independent valuation was not located. Parent loans to the subsidiary of ₹6.4141 crore and associate of ₹0.0835 crore have different consolidation treatment: the subsidiary loan is eliminated, not extra group cash. March auditor appointments concern internal/secretarial roles, not a statutory resignation. The 43,300 exercised options produced ₹45.465 lakh; 156,000 remaining options are modeled separately. Related parties and presentation limitations do not automatically establish an integrity failure. [S1][S5][S6][S7][S8][S10][S11]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: Group PAT in FY2024/FY2025/FY2026 was ₹15.3614/20.1756/19.6764 crore, compared with CFO of ₹0.1295/−17.4975/0.2156 crore. Cumulative CFO/PAT is −0.3107. Adding back the ₹2.2099 crore IPO-expense classification in FY2024 still leaves cumulative CFO at −₹14.9425 crore. Net cash capex was ₹1.5692/0.0782/9.8344 crore, producing three-year CFO less net capex of −₹28.6342 crore. FY2026 also used ₹0.632 crore of cash for capital advances. FY2025 net capex benefited from an asset disposal, so it is not a maintenance-spending benchmark. The FY2026 cash bridge is ₹30.4186 crore before WC + ₹7.5988 crore receivable release − ₹4.5847 crore advances − ₹1.1713 crore other assets − ₹23.1962 crore payables + ₹0.0328 crore other liabilities − ₹8.8824 crore cash tax = ₹0.2156 crore CFO. Both sides of working capital matter. Receivables of ₹104.5475 crore equal 54.61% of revenue; average-balance collection days are about 206.5. Balances over six months rose from ₹17.6559 crore to ₹26.9411 crore, including ₹4.0399 crore over three years. Headline cash of ₹21.0893 crore includes ₹19.7268 crore of deposits, of which ₹9.6997 crore is pledged; immediately available cash is ₹1.3625 crore. Gross debt of ₹29.4547 crore is about 1.03 times core EBITDA of ₹28.6949 crore; EBIT/finance cost of 18.46 times is comfortable historically but cannot prove intra-year liquidity. Group PAT is not owner PAT: ₹19.1685 crore after minority allocation less the ₹0.0255 crore associate loss gives calculated owner profit of ₹19.1430 crore. Reported EPS of ₹15.03 uses the group figure; calculated owner EPS is about ₹14.62 on weighted shares. Original FY2023 PBT/PAT/CFO of ₹9.9545/7.2767/0.9925 crore differ from IPO-restated ₹10.3711/7.6135/1.7652 crore; employee-cost restatement explains the PBT difference. These streams are not spliced. Financing invested capital, defined as equity + NCI + debt − cash − associate, rises from ₹12.8108 crore in FY2023 to ₹98.9580 crore in FY2026. Incremental normalized NOPAT/ΔIC is about 13.75%, and only about 5.86% over FY2024–FY2026. Retaining restricted deposits in the denominator lowers returns further. Every opening tax, employee, statutory, interest, capital-creditor and legacy claim has an explicit treatment in the model. [S1][S2][S3][S4]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: Market capitalization of ₹268.60 crore is 14.03 times calculated owner PAT or 13.65 times group PAT; those definitions are not interchangeable. Enterprise value is about ₹276.97 crore if all cash is deducted, or ₹296.69 crore if only immediately available cash is deducted, before economic minority claims. Against core EBITDA of ₹28.6949 crore, this implies 9.65–10.34 times, illustrating why restricted cash matters. The base exit multiple of 9 times EBITDA is an analyst normalization assumption, not a global-peer P/E comparison. Five post-entry periods end on 19 October 2031. Base growth is 20/15/12/10/8%, EBITDA margin 14%, capex 2.5% of sales, debt cost 10.5% and normalized tax 26%. Bear growth is −10/3/5/5/5%, margin 10%, receivable intensity seven percentage points higher, supplier credit 2.5 points lower, debt cost 13% and exit multiple 6. Bull growth is 35/25/20/15/12%, margin 15%, receivables three points lower and exit multiple 11. Each scenario links cash, tax, debt, capex, working capital, legacy claims, deposits, options and minority claims. Bear/base/bull terminal prices are ₹91.14/343.71/622.57, producing annualized returns of −14.93%/10.94%/24.93%; no probabilities are asserted. Base hurdle entry values are ₹170.89 at 15%, ₹195.03 at 12% and ₹150.24 at 18%. These are conditional valuation references, not orders or allocation advice. Base R is 3, just below the 11% IRR boundary for R 4. Reserve, minority, capex, funding and collection sensitivities can cross that boundary. At a 14% margin and 9-times exit multiple, a constant 18.67% revenue CAGR is needed for a 15% return, compared with about 12.93% in the slowing base path. Full annual scenarios, reverse expectations and sensitivities accompany the valuation. [S1][S6][S11][S12][S16]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The strongest bear argument is that an apparently profitable services company must continually finance government receivables while paying suppliers sooner. A modest margin miss combined with delayed collections can absorb internal cash. Accounting profit and a low trailing P/E do not assure liquidity or shareholder recovery. The ordinary bear case assumes a 10% initial revenue decline, a 10% EBITDA margin, receivables seven percentage points higher and supplier credit 2.5 points lower. It repays annual-end debt eventually, but the ₹91.14 exit price loses 55.45% of entry capital. Severe stress combines a 25% initial revenue decline, 7% margin, loss of 20% of opening receivables, receivable intensity 13 points higher, supplier credit five points lower, no initial deposit release, 15% debt cost, earlier legacy settlement and a ₹2 crore additional claim. Annual-end debt reaches ₹77.57 crore and residual equity is zero at a 4-times exit multiple. This is a linked downside scenario, not a forecast of default or an issuer finding. The ₹40 crore funding comparison is an analyst reference, not a verified sanctioned facility. Intra-year needs could be higher. Separate tests cover zero tax-credit recovery, ₹5 crore additional capex, larger minority participation and preference claims. No tax shield is assumed for the receivable impairment. [S1][S4][S11]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Fivefold and tenfold share-price outcomes over five years require approximately 47.6% and 71.7% constant annual revenue growth under the base 14% margin, 9-times exit multiple and linked funding, option and minority assumptions. The resulting revenue is approximately ₹1,340 crore and ₹2,858 crore, versus audited revenue of ₹191.44 crore and the demonstrated three-year CAGR of 17.09%. This is mathematically possible but commercial access, delivery throughput and financing at that scale are not established. Management’s ₹1,000 crore FY2030 aspiration does not by itself justify a fivefold stock return: extra sales require working capital, and economic value must accrue to diluted owners. A higher exit multiple would reduce the growth requirement while substituting valuation risk for operating proof. No multibagger designation is assigned. [S1][S5]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: This is a research checklist, not automated monitoring. First, compare revenue with management’s FY2027 ₹300–325 crore target and reconcile binding backlog, cancellations and execution separately from the ₹500–550 crore pipeline. Second, test actual collection of the ₹26.94 crore of receivables older than six months; an increase above ₹30 crore without credible receipts is a warning. Third, seek sustained improvement from three-year CFO/PAT of −0.31 toward 0.8, without relying on delayed supplier payments. Fourth, track operating WC near 40% of sales: a five-point receivable increase plus two-point supplier-credit compression pushes modeled debt beyond ₹40 crore. Fifth, obtain current limits, covenants, pledged deposits and monthly cash peaks; EBIT interest coverage below three times would trigger a funding review. Sixth, verify external deployment of the ₹2 crore subsidiary-investment proceeds, not just an intragroup transfer. Seventh, check Wardha completion and Kanjli milestones, O&M obligations and receipts. Eighth, distinguish Shiva sponsorship cash from project cost and profit. Ninth, refresh remaining options, new issuance, CCPS rights and subsidiary minority earnings. Tenth, verify lot size, traded values, depth, circuits and current restrictions before implementation. [S1][S5][S6][S7][S8][S9][S11][S19]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: The v3.0 matrix classifies this as Weak setup / value-trap risk because BQS 5.04 is between 4 and 6 and IAS 3.71 is below 5.5. It is not Avoid—governance, and no current funding failure has been demonstrated. It is not a compounder: BQS below 8, GQS below 7, CASH 2 and unproven severe-stress funding fail the designation. A price near ₹171 would meet the base model’s 15% hurdle only if its operating, collection, funding and minority assumptions hold. A lower price alone would not repair cash quality or establish an attractive risk-adjusted setup. The analytical action is an evidence watch rather than an unconditional new-purchase case. Improvements would require actual cash conversion, verified capital structure and financing, delivery of delayed projects and less demanding price-implied expectations. Rankings remain provisional among completed research; there is no final ranking of all 457 instruments or suitability judgment for the user’s portfolio. [S1][S2][S5][S16]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Evidence prioritizes the complete issuer FY2026 annual report, older annual reports, IPO restatement, allotment and utilization filings, dated awards, the earnings call and official NSE data. The available NSE annual-report copy ended before the complete consolidated statements; the issuer’s 149-page copy supplied them. An extraction problem is not issuer non-disclosure. The undated intake CSV is not current truth. Genuine gaps include October balances and sanctioned headroom; precise organic/price/volume mix; current customer and vendor concentration; a complete backlog bridge; post-March project collections; live trading depth; updated CCPS conversion terms; subsidiary economic valuation; and independent resolution of historical legal matters. The model conservatively retains ₹2 crore of unused IPO cash without terminal credit and tests a zero-reserve alternative. This is a valuation bound, not an assertion of permanent legal restriction. A common-minority allocation of 3% of group residual equity is not an ownership-matched subsidiary valuation; 0%, 6% and 10% alternatives are tested. Separate preference bounds of ₹0, ₹0.088, ₹1 and ₹5 crore address historical ₹0.08 crore principal and uncertain conversion value. The ₹0.088 crore case includes five years of 2% accrual; existing ₹0.0128 crore cumulative dividend is already in the legacy claim and is not charged twice. Unpublished movements are not represented as facts. These qualifications support a conditional Medium-confidence analysis, not exact entity-level financing certification. [S1][S4][S11][S16]

GOV.reason: FY2026 audited no-default findings and named related-party disclosures support adequate stewardship. The unused ₹2 crore IPO object and unverified fairness of a ₹1.75 crore prior director asset sale limit a stronger capital-allocation judgment. Contrary evidence: these disclosed dealings are not proof of abuse, and March auditor changes concern internal and secretarial roles, not a statutory resignation.

MOAT.reason: Design credentials and tender qualifications help win complex public projects; dated Wardha and Kanjli awards corroborate access. Fixed-price tenders and competing event providers make the advantage contestable. Contrary evidence: demonstrated delivery access is more valuable than a completely undifferentiated commodity service, but no verified premium or market share proves a structural moat.

REV.reason: The chosen comparable FY2023–FY2026 revenue CAGR is 17.09%, giving a starting score of 7. The 98.45% five-year CAGR is dominated by the pandemic base and is not scored. Latest growth slowed to 11.59%, but revenue still increased ₹19.89 crore and there is insufficient sustained comparable evidence for a trajectory adjustment. Organic price and volume mix are not separately quantified; Medium confidence limits any historical score to 8.

DUR.reason: Named museum/tourism awards and commercial sponsorship support several accessible growth avenues, including longer operations. Public budgets, seasonal events, cancellation risk and unverified pipeline conversion constrain persistence. Contrary evidence: the runway is not based solely on a large market estimate, because specific recent contracts exist.

CAP.reason: FY2023–FY2026 incremental normalized return of about 13.75% falls within the assumed 11–15% capital-cost range; FY2024–FY2026 is only about 5.86% as capital absorption grows. Contrary evidence: current operating profit remains strong and later collections could improve returns. Mixed returns support 5, not an allegation of permanent value destruction or exceptional reinvestment economics.

CASH.reason: Three profitable years generated cumulative CFO of −₹17.15 crore against ₹55.21 crore of group PAT. Receivables older than six months increased despite lower total receivables. Contrary evidence: FY2026 CFO became slightly positive and receivables released ₹7.60 crore, but supplier payments consumed ₹23.20 crore. Even the IPO-expense classification adjustment leaves cumulative CFO negative. Persistent weakness supports 2 and the GQS cap.

BAL.reason: Gross debt of ₹29.45 crore is about 1.03 times core EBITDA and the audit reports no default. Restricted deposits and large receivables make headline cash misleading as immediate repayment capacity. Severe collection and supplier-credit stress requires ₹77.57 crore of modeled annual-end debt, with facilities unverified. Contrary evidence: the ordinary bear repays debt without an assumed rescue; severe stress alone does not prove a present funding failure.

EXEC.reason: Revenue scaled across three years and new named awards show delivery capability. FY2026 revenue nevertheless missed the prior ₹225–240 crore target, while management’s ₹35 crore deferral explanation is not yet verified through execution. Contrary evidence: revenue still grew; this is mixed performance, not a claim of repeated unexplained failure.

EARN.reason: Core EBIT increased from about ₹10.75 crore in original FY2023 to ₹26.76 crore in FY2026, driven mainly by operations rather than other income. Latest group PAT declined 2.47% and reported EPS fell from ₹15.42 to ₹15.03; owner attribution differs from group PAT. Contrary evidence: core EBIT still grew about 5.35%. Cash realization is assessed separately, not penalized twice here.

R.reason: Conditional base IRR of 10.9376% minus the 15% equity hurdle gives a spread of −4.0624 percentage points and R 3. The result is close to the −4-point boundary; IPO-reserve or minority alternatives can move the score to 4. These are transparent sensitivities, not forecast certainty.

D.reason: The ordinary bear exits near ₹91.14, losing about 55.45% of capital. Severe stress produces zero residual equity and a ₹77.57 crore annual-end debt requirement, exceeding the illustrative ₹40 crore reference. Contrary evidence: the ordinary bear remains funded in the annual model. The score reflects loss severity and financing risk, not a repeated penalty for the base return.

P.reason: At a 14% margin and 9-times exit multiple, the 15% hurdle requires about 18.67% constant revenue CAGR plus collection and financing execution, stronger than the slowing base path. Minority and working-capital misses reduce returns. Contrary evidence: modestly declining revenue can preserve nominal capital in the model; the current price does not require the ₹1,000 crore aspiration simply to avoid loss.

L.reason: The ₹5 lakh reference divided by 5% of ₹13.8622 lakh conservative daily turnover gives 7.21 days, starting at L 5. One combined downgrade to 4 reflects the ₹81,820 minimum lot and sparse-participant/irregular-trading alerts. Contrary evidence: trades were observed in 57 of 60 sessions and the SM series is eligible. Missing live depth prevents an execution guarantee, not a coarse historical score.

method_notes: Unutilized IPO subsidiary investment proceeds of2crore are retained as purpose-restricted reserve in all core cases, without separate terminal addition. Group downstream investment is not a second expense. A zero-reserve sensitivity covers release/deployment within modeled capex or overlap with already-retained collateral; exact overlap and utilization after March2026 are unverified.

Forecast periods run19October2026–19October2031, not fiscal years. Last audited31March2026 balances are an explicit conditional opening-balance proxy; unreported April–October collections, profits and obligations are not fabricated. The model therefore is not a verified19October balance sheet or current-year earnings estimate. Known declared dividend is charged once conservatively; timing-delay tests shift the same terminal payoff to5.5/6years without claiming faster earnings realization.
Base20% initial growth is below management FY2027 target300–325crore; subsequent slowdown and14% margin are analyst assumptions. Pipeline is not backlog; contracts are not added again to revenue.
Recurring employee/ESOP expense remains in EBITDA without addback; known remaining156000 options add cash at105 when exercised, unlike already-issued43300 shares. More issuance is not assumed.

FY2026 balances are read from visual tables, not OCR alone. Ordinary liabilities scale consistently with sales. Noncurrent legacy claims are separately retained/settled. Tax credits are neither WC nor duplicate cash tax relief.

Terminal9xEBITDA applies to earnings after operating rent and recurring benefit cost; operating assets, security deposits and restricted FD are not added a second time. No separate goodwill/IP resale value.

Minority3% of group residual equity is an explicit common-equity allocation approximation based on subsidiary ownership and latest profit contribution, bounded at0–6%; it is not a claim that the subsidiary is wholly owned. Book NCI is not deducted twice. The3% claim is not ownership-matched subsidiary valuation. CCPS terms remain unverified after IPO; separate0.088crore nominal-plus-accrual bound and0/1/5crore sensitivities prevent presenting it as reconciled redemption value.

The40crore lending envelope is a disclosed analyst stress reference, not sanction confirmation. Report peak debt and envelope exceedance rather than implying unlimited finance. Base and stress solvency remain conditional on access and timing; no proven default is inferred.
